capabilities: Chat about the current note or selected text from editing, reading, and Web Viewer contexts
Search vault notes locally with BM25 and send the highest-ranked excerpts as context
Fetch web search results via DuckDuckGo or Tavily and combine them with note context
Display which selections, notes, vault results, and web candidates were sent to the model
Connect to any OpenAI-compatible service, including local endpoints
disambiguation: Not a vault search tool; the local BM25 search exists to supply context for AI conversations.
extras: The interface is currently available only in Simplified Chinese. The Web Viewer selection hook is desktop-only, though the rest works on mobile. Keys are stored in Obsidian SecretStorage rather than data.json. The manifest notes the plugin has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff. The README includes a privacy disclosure: questions and enabled note excerpts are sent directly to the configured model endpoint, and search queries go to DuckDuckGo or Tavily.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in AI chat, and existing AI plugins typically require an embedding service or a specific provider instead of an arbitrary OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

relations.evidence: Connect to OpenAI-compatible services, including local endpoints.
Use DuckDuckGo without a search API key, or configure Tavily.
If web search is enabled, the query is sent to DuckDuckGo or Tavily

requires.name: Tavily key (if Tavily web search is chosen)

summary: AI sidebar that chats with selected text, the current note, BM25-ranked vault notes, and web results using your own OpenAI-compatible API.
